title: Rise of the AI Architect — Clay Bavor, Cofounder, Sierra w/ Alessio Fanelli
talk_summary: Clay Bavor describes Sierra's customer-facing agent platform and the emerging 'AI architect' role, emphasizing non-deterministic software lifecycles, simulation-based testing, and closed-loop coaching of agents.

takeaways.what_they_do: Before going live they generate dozens of simulated personas/accounts/devices and run tens or hundreds of thousands of simulated conversations against the agent to surface gaps and corner cases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we've built a whole user simulation testing harness where we can create dozens of different personas with simulated accounts
takeaways.numbers: tens or hundreds of thousands of conversations before first launch

takeaways.technique: Regression + model-migration testing as first-class lifecycle steps
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat regression testing, unit testing, and model migration/upgrades as core parts of the 'agent development life cycle' rather than afterthoughts, because the software is non-deterministic.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how do you do regression testing and unit testing? How do you do model migration and model upgrades?

takeaways.what_they_do: Bavor keeps a Google Doc of problems that were too hard for older models and periodically re-tests them against new models to plot capability/latency/cost trends and build to where the puck is going.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I keep in a Google doc some problems that were too hard right for GBT T4 to solve

takeaways.what_they_do: They give CX/eng teams tools to inspect where the agent failed or handed off, then feed those cases back to coach and improve the agent in an 'upward spiral'.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent can learn from its past mistakes. It can be coached. It can be improved
takeaways.numbers: a team reviewing a couple hundred conversations a day

takeaways.technique: Start narrow, celebrate small end-to-end wins
takeaways.what_they_do: They advise starting with one concrete narrow problem (e.g., processing a single return) and expanding, rather than a broad 'apply AI' strategy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: start with a concrete valuable problem to solve and it can be very narrow

takeaways.what_they_do: They let the agent flex on curveballs but force fully deterministic behavior where hallucination is unacceptable (compliance/regulatory language).
takeaways.evidence_quote: down to fully deterministic where needed like there's no hallucinating you know compliance regula
